C) 'anterior fragment to be displaced backwards by action of the temporalis muscle.' The temporalis muscle primarily acts on the coronoid process and ramus (part of the posterior fragment) to elevate and retract. It would not primarily displace the anterior fragment backwards.
D) 'posterior fragment to be displaced medially by action of the medial pterygoid muscle.' The medial pterygoid muscle attaches to the medial surface of the angle and ramus and can pull the posterior fragment medially, as well as upwards and anteriorly. This is also a plausible displacement.

While flaccid paralysis would be immediate and continuous, atrophy is a progressive structural change that becomes very pronounced and characteristic over a 6-month period of denervation.
